title: Evolutionary history strongly structures brood-level mixed paternity across birds
text:
0.1 Updated analytical dataset
All results on this page use the models after exclusion of the two records for the common ostrich (6/6) and Nelson’s sparrow (8/8), whose exact counts could not be verified as broods with at least two genetic sires. Other records were retained, including the saltmarsh-sparrow record from the same Walsh study. Updated 5 November 2026.
The overall model contains 617 records, 553 study identifiers and 373 species. The primary multivariable model contains 531 records, 480 study identifiers and 324 species.
The estimated mean prevalence of mixed paternity was 31.6% (95% CrI: 11.8–57.2%), averaged over the fitted study and species random-effect distributions. Calculation and detailed results (updated 6 November 2026).

title: 3  Data preparation
text:
3.2 Import data

3.2.1 The input files used in the analysis: the mixed-paternity dataset and the dated Clements phylogenetic tree.

data_file <- "mixed_pat_final.csv"
tree_file <- "summary_dated_clements.nex"

mixed_pat_raw <- readr::read_csv(data_file, show_col_types = FALSE)
tree <- ape::read.nexus(tree_file)
This table summarises the curated input dataset and the phylogenetic tree.
The input CSV is the curated database: 676 records grouped under 607 distinct study identifiers (Study_ID), covering 393 species. The manuscript documents its derivation from 702 assembled records after removal of 26 overlapping records. Excluding 57 records without the required outcome or denominator leaves 619 records; exclusion of the two ambiguous records then leaves 617 analytical records, 553 study identifiers and 373 species. Thus, 607 and 553 refer to different dataset stages. The supplement lists 608 distinct source-publication entries for the broader curated database; bibliographic entries and analytical study identifiers are different counting units.
The updated literature search has a separate counting sequence: 2,288 identified bibliographic records minus 623 duplicates gives 1,665 screened records; excluding 1,476 at title/abstract screening leaves 189 reports for full-text assessment. Of these, 46 were excluded and 143 reports were included. Reports are source documents, not unique analytical study identifiers or database rows. See the updated search flow diagram.

data_summary <- tibble::tibble(
  Item = c("Curated dataset", "Phylogenetic tree"),
  Summary = c(
    paste0(nrow(mixed_pat_raw), " rows and ", ncol(mixed_pat_raw), " columns"),
    paste0(length(tree$tip.label), " tips and ", tree$Nnode, " internal nodes")
  )
)

knitr::kable(data_summary)

title: 3  Data preparation
text:
3.3 Prepare data

3.3.1 Population identifier
Population identity was defined using study identity and rounded geographic coordinates, with latitude and longitude rounded to two decimal places prior to constructing the population identifier.

mixed_pat <- mixed_pat_raw %>%
  mutate(
    Lat_round = round(Lat, 2),
    Long_round = round(Long, 2),
    population_id = paste(Study_ID, Lat_round, Long_round, sep = "_"),
    population_id = as.factor(population_id)
  )


3.3.2 Study and species formatting
The following step formats the main grouping variables used in the models and calculates the total number of broods by combining mixed- and non-mixed-brood counts.

mixed_pat <- mixed_pat %>%
  mutate(
    Study_ID = as.factor(Study_ID),
    species_phylo_brms = as.factor(Clements_name),
    species_nonphylo = as.factor(Clements_name),

    n_mixed_broods = as.numeric(n_mixed_broods),
    n_non_mixed_broods = as.numeric(n_non_mixed_broods),
    n_total_broods = n_mixed_broods + n_non_mixed_broods
  )


3.3.3 Phylogeny preparation
Species names were harmonised between the mixed-paternity dataset and the phylogenetic tree prior to pruning the tree and generating the phylogenetic covariance matrix used in the Bayesian models.

species_data <- mixed_pat %>%
  filter(!is.na(species_phylo_brms)) %>%
  pull(species_phylo_brms) %>%
  as.character() %>%
  unique()

species_tree <- tree$tip.label

species_for_tree <- intersect(species_data, species_tree)

tree_analysis <- ape::keep.tip(tree, species_for_tree)

phylo_mat <- ape::vcv.phylo(tree_analysis, corr = TRUE)

phylo_mat <- phylo_mat[
  sort(rownames(phylo_mat)),
  sort(colnames(phylo_mat))
]

mixed_pat <- mixed_pat %>%
  filter(species_phylo_brms %in% rownames(phylo_mat)) %>%
  mutate(
    species_phylo_brms = droplevels(species_phylo_brms),
    species_nonphylo = droplevels(species_nonphylo)
  )


3.3.4 Phylogeny - summary

phylo_summary <- tibble::tibble(
  Item = c(
    "Species matched to phylogeny",
    "Tips in source tree",
    "Species retained after phylogenetic filtering"
  ),
  Value = c(
    length(species_for_tree),
    length(tree$tip.label),
    n_distinct(mixed_pat$species_phylo_brms)
  )
)

knitr::kable(phylo_summary)


3.3.5 Moderator variable preparation

min_n <- 5

mixed_pat <- mixed_pat %>%
  mutate(
    marker_type_model = as.factor(marker_type_model),
    nest_box_model = as.factor(nest_box_model),
    nest_type_model = as.factor(nest_type_model),

    breeding_system = as.factor(breeding_system),
    mono_poly_model = as.factor(mono_poly_model),
    parental_care = as.factor(parental_care),
    cooperative_breeding = as.factor(cooperative_breeding),

    migration = as.factor(migration),
    coloniality = as.factor(coloniality),

    CS_max = as.numeric(CS_max),
    body_mass = as.numeric(body_mass),
    study_duration = as.numeric(study_duration_num),

    Lat_round = round(as.numeric(Lat), 2),
    abs_lat = abs(Lat_round)
  )

title: 3  Data preparation
text:
3.4 Preparation of the database

3.4.1 Database overall study

data_overall_study <- mixed_pat %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(n_mixed_broods),
    !is.na(n_non_mixed_broods),
    !is.na(n_total_broods),
    n_total_broods > 0,
    !is.na(Study_ID),
    !is.na(species_phylo_brms)
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    Study_ID = droplevels(Study_ID),
    species_nonphylo = droplevels(species_nonphylo),
    species_phylo_brms = droplevels(species_phylo_brms),
    population_id = droplevels(population_id)
  )


3.4.2 Common scaling of continuous moderators
The centring and scaling constants are calculated once from the 619-record overall analytical dataset, before moderator-specific complete-case filtering. The same constants are then reused in every single-moderator and multivariable analysis.

data_overall_study <- data_overall_study %>%
  mutate(
    log_body_mass = replace(
      body_mass,
      !is.na(body_mass) & body_mass <= 0,
      NA_real_
    ),
    log_body_mass = log10(log_body_mass)
  )

scaling_constants <- data_overall_study %>%
  summarise(
    study_duration_mean = mean(study_duration, na.rm = TRUE),
    study_duration_sd = sd(study_duration, na.rm = TRUE),
    CS_max_mean = mean(CS_max, na.rm = TRUE),
    CS_max_sd = sd(CS_max, na.rm = TRUE),
    log_body_mass_mean = mean(log_body_mass, na.rm = TRUE),
    log_body_mass_sd = sd(log_body_mass, na.rm = TRUE),
    abs_lat_mean = mean(abs_lat, na.rm = TRUE),
    abs_lat_sd = sd(abs_lat, na.rm = TRUE)
  )

data_overall_study <- data_overall_study %>%
  mutate(
    study_duration_sc =
      (study_duration - scaling_constants$study_duration_mean) /
      scaling_constants$study_duration_sd,
    CS_max_sc =
      (CS_max - scaling_constants$CS_max_mean) /
      scaling_constants$CS_max_sd,
    log_body_mass_sc =
      (log_body_mass - scaling_constants$log_body_mass_mean) /
      scaling_constants$log_body_mass_sd,
    abs_lat_sc =
      (abs_lat - scaling_constants$abs_lat_mean) /
      scaling_constants$abs_lat_sd
  )

scaling_table <- tibble::tribble(
  ~Predictor, ~N, ~Mean, ~SD, ~Unit,
  "Study duration", sum(!is.na(data_overall_study$study_duration)),
    scaling_constants$study_duration_mean, scaling_constants$study_duration_sd, "years",
  "Maximum clutch size", sum(!is.na(data_overall_study$CS_max)),
    scaling_constants$CS_max_mean, scaling_constants$CS_max_sd, "eggs",
  "Body mass", sum(!is.na(data_overall_study$log_body_mass)),
    scaling_constants$log_body_mass_mean, scaling_constants$log_body_mass_sd, "log10(g)",
  "Absolute latitude", sum(!is.na(data_overall_study$abs_lat)),
    scaling_constants$abs_lat_mean, scaling_constants$abs_lat_sd, "degrees"
) %>%
  mutate(across(c(Mean, SD), ~ round(.x, 3)))

knitr::kable(scaling_table)


3.4.3 Database single moderators

data_nest_box <- data_overall_study %>%
  filter(!is.na(nest_box_model)) %>%
  droplevels()


data_migration <- data_overall_study %>%
  filter(!is.na(migration)) %>%

data_cooperative <- data_overall_study %>%
  filter(!is.na(cooperative_breeding)) %>%
  droplevels()

data_study_duration <- data_overall_study %>%
  filter(!is.na(study_duration_sc)) %>%
  droplevels()

data_clutch_size <- data_overall_study %>%
  filter(!is.na(CS_max_sc)) %>%
  droplevels()

data_body_mass <- data_overall_study %>%
  filter(
    is.finite(log_body_mass),
    is.finite(log_body_mass_sc)
  ) %>%
  droplevels()

data_abs_latitude <- data_overall_study %>%
  filter(!is.na(abs_lat_sc)) %>%
  droplevels()

data_marker_type <- data_overall_study %>%
  filter(!is.na(marker_type_model)) %>%
  droplevels()


data_nest_type <- data_overall_study %>%
  filter(!is.na(nest_type_model)) %>%
  droplevels()


valid_breeding_levels <- data_overall_study %>%
  count(breeding_system) %>%
  filter(!is.na(breeding_system), n >= 5) %>%
  pull(breeding_system)

data_breeding_system <- data_overall_study %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(breeding_system),
    breeding_system %in% valid_breeding_levels
  ) %>%
  droplevels()

data_mono_poly <- data_overall_study %>%
  filter(!is.na(mono_poly_model)) %>%
  droplevels()

data_parental_care <- data_overall_study %>%
  filter(!is.na(parental_care)) %>%
  droplevels()

section: 3.5 Relationship among candidate random-effects grouping factors
text:
3.5 Relationship among candidate random-effects grouping factors
Before fitting the models, we evaluated the degree of overlap and nesting among candidate random-effects grouping factors, including species identity, study identity, and the pragmatic population identifier.

count_one_match <- function(data, group_var, match_var, comparison_label) {
  data %>%
    distinct({{ group_var }}, {{ match_var }}) %>%
    count({{ group_var }}, name = "n_matches") %>%
    summarise(
      Comparison = comparison_label,
      Groups_with_only_one_match = sum(n_matches == 1),
      Total_groups = n(),
      Percent_only_one_match = round(mean(n_matches == 1) * 100, 1),
      .groups = "drop"
    )
}

random_effect_structure <- bind_rows(
  count_one_match(data_overall_study, species_nonphylo, population_id, "Populations per species"),
  count_one_match(data_overall_study, population_id, species_nonphylo, "Species per population"),
  count_one_match(data_overall_study, Study_ID, population_id, "Populations per reference"),
  count_one_match(data_overall_study, population_id, Study_ID, "References per population"),
  count_one_match(data_overall_study, species_nonphylo, Study_ID, "References per species"),
  count_one_match(data_overall_study, Study_ID, species_nonphylo, "Species per reference")
)

title: 3  Data preparation
section: 3.7 Overlap between nest-box use and nest type (Table S7)
text:
3.7 Overlap between nest-box use and nest type (Table S7)
This descriptive table uses the overall analytical dataset prepared in this chapter: 575 of its 619 records have both nest-box use and nest type available. The remaining 44 records have missing information for one or both variables. Counts refer to records, not unique species or publications. This is a different sample from the 533 complete cases used for the primary multivariable model and Tables S5 and S8.
Of the 165 nest-box records, 119 (72.1%) were classified as cavity nesting. Nest type is included in the primary multivariable model, whereas nest-box use was evaluated in a separate single-moderator model. The table describes overlap between these candidate variables; it does not estimate their independent associations with mixed paternity.

summarise_nest_box_overlap <- function(data_overall_study) {
  required <- c("nest_box_model", "nest_type_model")
  stopifnot(nrow(data_overall_study) == 619L,
            all(required %in% names(data_overall_study)))
  complete <- complete.cases(data_overall_study[required])
  dat <- data_overall_study[complete, required, drop = FALSE]
  stopifnot(nrow(dat) == 575L, sum(!complete) == 44L)
  box_levels <- c("no", "yes")
  nest_levels <- c("cavity", "ground", "open", "other_enclosed")
  stopifnot(all(as.character(dat$nest_box_model) %in% box_levels),
            all(as.character(dat$nest_type_model) %in% nest_levels))
  counts <- table(
    factor(dat$nest_box_model, levels = box_levels),
    factor(dat$nest_type_model, levels = nest_levels)
  )
  counts <- rbind(counts, Total = colSums(counts))
  counts <- cbind(counts, Total = rowSums(counts))
  stopifnot(counts["Total", "Total"] == 575L)
  data.frame(
    `Nest-box use` = c("No", "Yes", "Total"),
    Cavity = as.integer(counts[, "cavity"]),
    Ground = as.integer(counts[, "ground"]),
    Open = as.integer(counts[, "open"]),
    `Other enclosed` = as.integer(counts[, "other_enclosed"]),
    Total = as.integer(counts[, "Total"]),
    check.names = FALSE
  )
}

overlap_table <- summarise_nest_box_overlap(data_overall_study)
dir.create("tables", showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
write.csv(overlap_table, "tables/nest_box_nest_type_overlap.csv", row.names = FALSE)
knitr::kable(overlap_table, caption = "Table S7. Nest-box use by nest type in 575 complete records from the 619-record overall analytical dataset; 44 records with missing information are excluded.")
Download Table S7.

title: 4  Overall model
text:
4.1 Overall model
All results on this page use the models after exclusion of the two records for the common ostrich (6/6) and Nelson’s sparrow (8/8), whose exact counts could not be verified as broods with at least two genetic sires. Other records were retained, including the saltmarsh-sparrow record from the same Walsh study. Models updated 5 November 2026; marginal mean added 6 November 2026.
Estimates are posterior means with 95% equal-tailed credible intervals (CrI). Odds ratios are summarised after exponentiating each contrast draw. The overall marginal mean integrates over the fitted random-effect distributions. Conditional estimates at zero random effects are explicitly labelled for comparison. Continuous effects use the original common scaling constants, retained unchanged after exclusion. Mixed paternity refers to the source-derived brood-level measure described in Methods; source reporting sometimes used brood-level EPP without identifying sire number.
The estimated mean prevalence of mixed paternity was 31.6% (95% CrI: 11.8–57.2%). This marginal mean averages over the fitted distributions of study, non-phylogenetic species and phylogenetic species effects. The pooled raw proportion is 16,075 / 46,235 = 34.77%; it weights observations by their brood denominators and is a different summary.
617 records, 553 study identifiers and 373 species; 16075 mixed-paternity broods out of 46235 sampled broods.

title: 4  Overall model
text:
4.2 Averaging over random effects
For each of 20,000 joint posterior draws, we calculated
\[
\bar p_s = \int \operatorname{logit}^{-1}(\alpha_s + \sqrt{V_s}z)\varphi(z)\,dz,
\quad V_s=\sigma^2_{\mathrm{study},s}+\sigma^2_{\mathrm{nonphylo},s}+\sigma^2_{\mathrm{phylo},s}.
\]
Here, \(\varphi\) is the standard normal density. The phylogenetic covariance matrix has unit diagonal. We used 160-node Gaussian quadrature and summarised the resulting marginal probabilities by their posterior mean and 2.5th and 97.5th percentiles. Checks with 80 nodes and independent adaptive integration agreed to better than \(4\times10^{-9}\) in probability. Beta-binomial precision controls sampling dispersion and does not change the expected probability.
This estimates a mean under the fitted study and species distributions, not an empirical or census-weighted average of all birds. Moderator-specific curves and category predictions elsewhere remain conditional on zero random effects. No models were refitted for this calculation.

All results on this page use the models after exclusion of the two records for the common ostrich (6/6) and Nelson’s sparrow (8/8), whose exact counts could not be verified as broods with at least two genetic sires. Other records were retained, including the saltmarsh-sparrow record from the same Walsh study. Updated 5 November 2026.
Estimates are posterior means with 95% equal-tailed credible intervals (CrI). Odds ratios are summarised after exponentiating each contrast draw. Prevalence predictions are summarised after inverse-logit transformation, with random effects set to zero. Continuous effects use the original common scaling constants, retained unchanged after exclusion. Mixed paternity refers to the source-derived brood-level measure described in Methods; source reporting sometimes used brood-level EPP without identifying sire number.
612 records, 549 study identifiers and 371 species; 16047 mixed-paternity broods out of 46164 sampled broods.

title: 8  Multivariable model

8.1 Multivariable model
All results on this page use the models after exclusion of the two records for the common ostrich (6/6) and Nelson’s sparrow (8/8), whose exact counts could not be verified as broods with at least two genetic sires. Other records were retained, including the saltmarsh-sparrow record from the same Walsh study. Updated 5 November 2026.
Estimates are posterior means with 95% equal-tailed credible intervals (CrI). Odds ratios are summarised after exponentiating each contrast draw. Prevalence predictions are summarised after inverse-logit transformation, with random effects set to zero. Continuous effects use the original common scaling constants, retained unchanged after exclusion. Mixed paternity refers to the source-derived brood-level measure described in Methods; source reporting sometimes used brood-level EPP without identifying sire number.
531 records, 480 study identifiers and 324 species; 14903 mixed-paternity broods out of 41511 sampled broods.
